facts.text: I am trying to create a budget plan for my farm.
I have been doing pretty well selling produce at the farmer's market.
I sold a calf to a neighboring farm.
My total income has been around $3,500.
I have been tracking my expenses in a spreadsheet.
My total expenses for the past three months have been around $5,000.
My past three months of expenses include the cost of feed.
My past three months of expenses include vet bills.
My past three months of expenses include equipment costs.
I spent around $500 on new feeding troughs for the cows last week.
I spent around $120 on vet bills for Luna's broken wing.
I got a discount on a bulk purchase of hay.
The bulk purchase of hay should last for the next two months.
I have been selling around 20 dozen eggs at the farmer's market.
I have been selling around 5 pounds of fresh cheese made from the cow's milk at the farmer's market.
I priced the eggs at $3 per dozen.
I priced the cheese at $10 per pound.
My total revenue from the eggs and cheese was $160.
I wanted to adjust the Livestock Expenses category to reflect the $120 vet bill for Luna's broken wing.
I made a mistake and did not subtract the $500 feed expense from the total Livestock Expenses.
My Livestock Expenses total was $657.
In my revised Livestock Expenses breakdown, Vet bills were $120.
In my revised Livestock Expenses breakdown, Feed was $500.
In my revised Livestock Expenses breakdown, Breeding and genetics was $20.
In my revised Livestock Expenses breakdown, Other livestock-related expenses was $17.

keyphrases: selling a calf to neighboring farm
